title: Natural derived tensor comparison for independently localized open restriction
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U any open, and choose independently localized derived categories D(X), D(U) [def-pc-derived-category] with their fixed derived tensor structures [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. For exact derived open restriction R [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps], there is a natural isomorphism of bifunctors R(E tensor F) ≅ R(E) tensor R(F). There are no boundedness, quasi-coherence, separation or nonemptiness hypotheses.

source.place: Derived tensor construction; Tag 08EU first sentence (locality); K-flat model expansion of the tensor-restriction part.

proof.text: Use K-flat resolutions to compute both tensor inputs and the natural derived-tensor counit comparison. Restriction preserves K-flatness, so the restricted models also compute the local derived tensor.

Restriction commutes with the sheaf tensor and the sums in totalization. The total-tensor comparison is natural in both complex maps: the bidegree tensor naturality squares intertwine the horizontal and signed vertical differentials; the coproduct comparisons commute with maps into each summand. Its inverse is natural by cancellation.

Compose the total-tensor comparison with the K-flat derived counit comparisons. Use common K-flat refinements of quasi-isomorphism roofs to see that the result is independent of resolution and natural on derived morphisms. Full faithfulness of precomposition with the product derived localization then descends the comparison and inverse to a natural isomorphism. The exact restriction factorization isomorphism and uniqueness of localization transport it between independent localization universes. The empty open gives the same construction on zero models.

proof_origin.note: Natural bifunctor form of K-flat tensor restriction, allowing independent localization universes.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedTensor_openRestriction_natIso (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wO} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))] :
    let R := (schemeOpenRestriction X U).mapDerivedCategory
    Nonempty (tensor (schemeDerivedCategory X) ⋙ R ≅
      R.prod R ⋙ tensor (schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme))
